title: Where the Minutes Go in a Traditional School Day
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Estimate how many minutes of an illustrative 425-minute middle-school day are whole-class direct instruction, then reveal a chart of where the minutes go.

educational.topic: How time is used in a traditional school day
learningObjectives: The learner will differentiate the minutes of an illustrative middle-school day into whole-class direct instruction, practice, and non-instructional time, estimating the direct-instruction total to within 10 minutes.
prerequisites: School day, direct instruction, the I-do, we-do, you-do pattern, and classroom, from Chapter 1.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Estimate before the reveal, then compare with the data
keyQuestions: How many minutes of the day are whole-class direct instruction?
How much of the day is non-instructional?
commonMisconceptions: Most of the school day is spent with a teacher explaining new material
Almost all of a seven-hour day is academic time
Non-instructional time such as passing, lunch, and settling in is negligible
assessmentOpportunities: How many minutes of whole-class direct instruction are in the day?
Why is direct instruction not 7 times 50 minutes?

controls.name: Estimate (a)
controls.description: Type the minutes of whole-class direct instruction, from 0 to 425.

controls.name: Estimate (b)
controls.description: Choose the largest single use of time.

controls.name: Reveal the chart
controls.description: Scores both estimates and shows the chart.

controls.name: Chart bars
controls.description: Click a bar to highlight the schedule rows that make it up.

controls.name: Try again
controls.description: Clears the estimates and hides the chart.
